woman noun

also women, young woman, old woman, female

classical

Traupman 408

mulier, mulieris f.

noun, third declension

a woman (as opposed to a man); also a wife

mulier is the everyday word, often of a married woman; fēmina is the female of the species and the respectful word; a lady is mātrōna (see lady).

Other words

  • fēmina, fēminae f. — a woman, a female

    noun, first declension · also used · classical

  • muliercula, mulierculae f. — a little woman; a silly woman (belittling)

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 5.103: aquam ferentis mulierculae (Lewis & Short s.v. susurrus); Traupman 408; Traupman 410

    Traupman gives it for “young woman” and “young lady”; classically the diminutive is usually belittling or pitying, “a poor little woman”. For a girl or young woman, puella or virgō.

Examples

  • anus, anūs f.

    an old womanTraupman 408

See also lady, old woman.
